title: Canonical regular coefficient model maps are isomorphisms
statement: Fix a prime ell, a finite extension E of Q_ell, and a scheme isomorphism g:X to Y. On the small pro-etale sites use the completed regular coefficient sheaves R_T and their positive-exponent quotients B_{T,n}, n in N representing exponent n+1 [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use sectionwise inverse image with its actual coefficient ring isomorphisms [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image]. Define u_R:R_X to g^{-1}R_Y and u_n:B_{X,n} to g^{-1}B_{Y,n} by the inverse coefficient maps, sending one to one. Define reduction R_T tensor A_n to B_{T,n} by the transpose of the quotient projection under the normalized scalar adjunction [lem-weil-derived-scalar-extension-restriction-adjunction]; extend this to degree-zero complexes. Define kappa_n to be the specified inverse-image-to-pullback comparison on B_{Y,n}[0] [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. Then u_R is an isomorphism, and for each n, u_n, the reduction complex on Y, and kappa_n are isomorphisms. These are the concrete constructions canonicalCoefficientIntegralUnit, canonicalCoefficientFiniteUnit, canonicalCoefficientReductionComplex and canonicalCoefficientFiniteKappaComplex; the module also records the integral/finite comparison and projection constructions used by the parent.

source.place: Tags 03D6 and 08TC; the parent coefficient-comparison proof and the proved regular-unit APIs of lean/Sheaf/Paper/ConstantWeilStructure.lean.

proof.text: The integral and finite unit maps are, sectionwise, inverse coefficient ring isomorphisms followed by multiplication by one. Their underlying maps are bijective, so the faithful sheaf and presheaf functors reflect the asserted isomorphisms.

The normalized scalar-adjunction transpose of the coefficient quotient equals the finite regular-module isomorphism. Check this by the unit/counit equations and the image of the regular generator. Its single-complex map is consequently an isomorphism.

For kappa_n conjugate by the regular inverse-image and pullback isomorphisms. The specified tensor-unit comparison sends the regular generator to itself, so regular-source extensionality gives the identity. Cancel the two regular isomorphisms.

lean.statement:
theorem canonicalCoefficientModelMaps_isIso {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (g : X ⟶ Y) [IsIso g] :
    IsIso (canonicalCoefficientIntegralUnit l E g) ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ, IsIso (canonicalCoefficientFiniteUnit l E g n) ∧
        IsIso (canonicalCoefficientReductionComplex l E Y n) ∧
        IsIso (canonicalCoefficientFiniteKappaComplex l E g n)
